title: Fix the self-comparison assertion in firestore_listener_source_test.dart:153 — expect(x, equals(x)) always passes
why: Comparing a value to itself is always true regardless of what orderField holds. The test's own comment states the intent — verify 'every wired collection... must carry an explicit, recognised field' via the actual order field passed to listenToCollection — and the preceding expect (checking FirestoreListenerSource.orderFields[entry.collection] is not null) does real work, but this second line adds nothing. If a future change wires the wrong orderField to a collection (e.g. swaps two entries in the orderFields map), this test cannot catch it, undermining the FB-2-adjacent guarantee that every listener sorts by its intended recency field.
recommendation: Change to expect(entry.orderField, equals(FirestoreListenerSource.orderFields[entry.collection])) so the assertion checks the actual call-site value against the expected map entry.
acceptance_criteria: Deliberately wiring the wrong orderField constant to one collection in the source makes the test fail red

corrections: Downgraded severity P2 -> P3; core claim and quote fully verified accurate.
